races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race

runners_data.name: Zoar
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's consistent filly has won and placed on Good ground over 6f, making her course-and-distance profile strong; she is the confirmed pace-setter here, and while she is technically stepping into a lead role from a prominent base, her form suggests she can handle dictating from the front with Harnett's 3lb claim keeping the weight competitive.

runners_data.name: Nation Blaze
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this filly whose form reads 8th and 9th in her two runs, both on Going that should suit today; she is flagged as fading in finishes which is a significant concern in a sprint, and her 49-day absence plus moderate form figures make her difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Eyeconic
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for J A Stack on this hold-up filly whose sole run produced an 11th-place finish on identical Good ground over 6f; the fade-in-finish flag compounded by a last-of-11 run is a serious concern, though Heffernan's quality gives a sliver of hope if improvement arrives with experience.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: Has strong form at this course and trip — a winner over 6f Cork on Good and placed here too — and his five-run course record is his biggest asset; naturally a prominent racer, he is likely to find himself further back than ideal given the traffic ahead of him, which is a genuine tactical compromise for Wesley Joyce to manage.

runners_data.name: Fighting Tears
runners_data.note: A winner on debut over this identical course, distance and going is about as strong a profile tick as a 2yo can carry into any race; she wants to race prominently but the crowded forward positions mean W J Lee may have to be patient, yet her superior form figures make her the most dangerous challenger to Zoar if she can find a position close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Belle Parvenue
runners_data.note: Unraced and a complete unknown for the Eddie & Patrick Harty yard; Chris Hayes takes the mount which is a positive talent indicator, but with no form, no going information and a listed style of U, she cannot be assessed beyond the bare intrigue of a well-bred debutante on Good ground.

races.paceDynamic: Zoar is the one confirmed front runner here and, with just six runners on Good ground over six furlongs at Cork, she should be able to stride to the front unchallenged and set a sustainable, controlled tempo. Fighting Tears and The Scallionator are both genuine prominent types by nature but the pace map cannot accommodate all three in forward positions — Zoar is likeliest to actually secure the lead, with Fighting Tears probably slotting in second or third and The Scallionator forced wider or further back than ideal. That measured, single-setter pace over a sprint trip on Good ground is a classic setup for a horse who can sit just off the pace, travel comfortably, and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the final two furlongs. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position, and those redistribution compromises tilt the tactical advantage firmly toward a horse who can race prominently with cover and quicken off a genuine but unhurried pace — the prominent-to-winner profile benefits most here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zoar Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Zoar bowls along at a fair but uncontested pace and the field settles into their rhythm behind her.
scenarios.body: Zoar dictates from the front without any pressure, conserving energy through the middle portion before asserting in the final furlong on Going that suits her 2/2 similar-ground record; her Donnacha O'Brien stable is in form and Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim adds value.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Fighting Tears travels powerfully just off Zoar's shoulder and produces a stronger finish in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Fighting Tears, a course-and-distance winner on identical Going, is the most natural threat to Zoar if she travels with the pace and times her challenge from second or third; W J Lee is an astute judge of pace and could engineer the perfect position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Scallionator Forced Wide, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If The Scallionator, despite being pushed out of his natural position, settles better than expected and runs on strongly late.
scenarios.body: A six-furlong Cork form line of 1-2-2 on Good gives The Scallionator genuine claims on form, and if the pace is strong enough from Zoar to stretch the field, he could emerge from a deeper position to grab a place or more.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut/Dark Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Parvenue or Eyeconic, both relatively unknown quantities, produce a performance that outstrips their current profile.
scenarios.body: Belle Parvenue is unraced and a complete unknown, while Eyeconic's sole run ended in a distant finish but form can improve sharply with a first outing under the belt; either could outrun their position if the pace collapses late.

watchPoints.text: Zoar must be tracked from flag-fall — if she gets a clean lead at a measured pace, she is the controlling influence and any late challenger will need to be travelling exceptionally well to peg her back.

Fighting Tears is the most potent danger to Zoar on form but watch whether W J Lee can secure a forward pitch early; if she gets boxed in or loses a length at the break, her chance is materially reduced.

The Scallionator's natural instinct is to race up with the pace, but with Zoar and Fighting Tears also wanting forward positions, monitor how he jumps and whether Joyce can find a slot — a wide, detached run will compromise his chance significantly.

Nation Blaze and Eyeconic are both flagged for fading in finishes, so watch whether either of them shows early pace before the final two furlongs — if they do, they are unlikely to sustain it and may open up ground for closers behind them.

Belle Parvenue is the unknown quantity — watch her in the paddock and in the early strides for any sign of greenness or, conversely, natural athleticism that suggests she could outrun her debut price.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Gleneagles Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: Ar Son Na Cuise
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien runner with two outings, both finishing tenth or worse over seven furlongs on Good — drops back to six here, but the form offers no encouragement; genuine hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is squeezed further by the volume of slow-starters in this field, reducing the chance of a clean run through.

runners_data.name: El Domino
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains this one, who has form figures of 6 and 10 on Good going over six furlongs — modest but at least competitive at the trip; prominent racer who should travel within striking range of the pace duel and is better positioned stylistically than the hold-up types to benefit if Revelator and Marco Polo press each other into weakness.

runners_data.name: Jungle Wise
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Daniel James Murphy, ridden by Ben Coen — no going data available and lightly raced flag applies; unknown quantity whose style is unclassified, making form assessment impossible, but a fresh two-year-old with a strong jockey booking always warrants respect in this maiden context.

runners_data.name: Marco Polo
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's runner has one place from two starts, including a second on Good over six furlongs — the most directly relevant experience in the field; confirmed front-runner who will battle Revelator for the early lead and whose outcome largely depends on whether that duel costs him or whether he can assert and control.

runners_data.name: Moon Sand
runners_data.note: Two starts for Joseph Patrick O'Brien, both finishing ninth on Good ground over longer trips — stepping down to six furlongs is a question, not necessarily an answer; the fade-in-finish flag and deep hold-up style leave this runner structurally disadvantaged in a race where the rear is overcrowded.

runners_data.name: Revelator
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's charge has a third and a seventh from two runs over six furlongs on Good — the best tactical profile for a genuine front-runner with distance and going experience; returns after 60 days off and will need to show peak fitness, as a lay-off of that length at two can matter, but the course-and-distance form is a clear positive.

runners_data.name: Snapequus
runners_data.note: Third O'Brien entry, with form figures of 11 and 11 over seven furlongs on Good — deeply unencouraging; fade-in-finish flag and hold-up style combine to make this a very difficult winner to construct under any race shape, and the step down in trip does not obviously address the core problem.

runners_data.name: Tennesspeed
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner has been off 98 days since a single run finishing eleventh over six furlongs on Good — significant absence for a juvenile returning into this company; the lay-off is a major flag, the form is absent, and the hold-up style leaves it reliant on an unlikely pace collapse to get involved.

runners_data.name: Timucua Gold
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Noel Meade — strong jockey booking on a horse with one run, an eighth over seven furlongs on Good; dropping to six furlongs may sharpen the profile, and while the fade-in-finish tag is noted, Keane's ability to place a horse tactically from an unknown style base makes this marginally interesting as an unexposed type.

races.paceDynamic: Revelator and Marco Polo are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gate, creating a genuinely competitive early pace over six furlongs on Good ground at Cork. With two horses pushing each other from the outset, the gallop should be honest rather than dawdling, setting up a race that is run at a true tempo rather than a tactical crawl. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Ar Son Na Cuise is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield because the rear is congested with similarly slow-starting runners (Moon Sand, Snapequus, Tennesspeed), meaning none are likely to secure their most comfortable position. This pace shape — two front-runners pressing each other over a flat, straight six furlongs — classically favours prominent-to-mid-division horses who can track the pace without getting caught in the battle, then pick up the pieces if the leaders tie each other up late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace duel sets up closers
scenarios.trigger: If Revelator and Marco Polo press each other hard from the gates and both fade inside the final furlong, horses tracking just off the pace inherit a clear run.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel between the two front-runners burns their reserves on Good ground over six furlongs, leaving a vacuum for horses sitting two to three lengths off the pace to sprint through; prominent types who avoid the battle while staying close enough to capitalise are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner dictates solo
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace horses — most likely Marco Polo — asserts early and Revelator drops away, a lone leader controls tempo and builds an unassailable lead.
scenarios.body: A solo pace-setter on Good ground over a flat six furlongs at Cork can regulate their own rhythm, avoiding the energy cost of a duel and quickening clear in the final two furlongs; Marco Polo's second-place finish on Good going is the most relevant formline in this context.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent stalker pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and a fresh, unexposed horse tracks just off the leaders without being caught in traffic.
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced type sitting third or fourth in the first half of the race benefits most here, able to use the strong pace as a springboard and produce a sustained late run through a tiring field; Jungle Wise and Timucua Gold, both with limited form, could be unexposed enough to do this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up closers pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the entire field strings out, creating a late-finishing opportunity for deep hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This scenario relies on Ar Son Na Cuise, Moon Sand, Snapequus or Tennesspeed producing sustained finishes, but all four hold-up types are mapped out of role and all carry flat or deeply unencouraging recent form with multiple last-placed finishes; this shape is the least likely to deliver given the structural constraints.

watchPoints.text: If Marco Polo and Revelator are separated by less than a length early, the duel is on — watch their head-to-head through the first two furlongs as the intensity of that battle will determine whether the race sets up for a prominent tracker or a front-runner.

Tennesspeed returns after 98 days off for Mrs Harrington — watch the market closely; a well-backed debutante or long-absent juvenile in a maiden can signal stable confidence that the form book cannot show.

Jungle Wise is an unraced unknown quantity for Daniel James Murphy with Ben Coen booked — if this runner moves freely early and travels prominently, treat as a live dark horse whose ceiling is undefined.

Joseph Patrick O'Brien saddles three runners (Ar Son Na Cuise, Moon Sand, Snapequus) — all hold-up types, all with poor recent form; watch whether any show signs of a changed ride or new tactics under their jockeys, as a stable with three in the race may have a stable order that is not obvious on paper.

El Domino is 37 days since last run with a prominent style and direct course-and-distance experience — if Seamie Heffernan settles him smoothly in fourth or fifth tracking the pace duel, note his position turning for home as the race shape may funnel directly to him.

races.name: Follow Us On Instagram Handicap

runners_data.name: Sommelier
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a win over 6f on good going in the past five starts, but the flagged finishing fade is a real concern in a big field where the late run may find traffic rather than clear air; 43 days off.|

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up sprinter with four places from his last 15 on good going — consistent without winning, but Cork 6f on good ground is squarely in his wheelhouse and he handles the conditions well.|

runners_data.name: Real Encounter
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old from the Harrington yard; Shane Foley in the saddle is a significant advantage in a chaotic race and the horse has placed at 5f and 6f on good ground, though a 53-day absence needs noting.|

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form is all over a mile and further — stepping back sharply to 6f on this evidence looks like a puzzle piece that doesn't quite fit.|

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old whose best going figures come on standard rather than good turf; 25 days since last run and no win to speak of, so this is a speculative each-way profile at best.|

runners_data.name: Whiskey And Beer
runners_data.note: Flagged fader who has been off the track for 760 days — the return from such a long absence with a fade tendency is a major red flag in a competitive 25-runner sprint.|

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Experienced hold-up veteran who won his most recent 6f on good going and has the strongest closing profile in the race; Ben Coen takes over and the 94-day break is the only mild concern.|

runners_data.name: Tornado Kiss
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old who won over 5f on good going and is trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery — up in trip and in distance here, but the 98-day layoff makes it hard to be confident.|

runners_data.name: Mehman
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature, squeezed into a midfield map position because true hold-up slots are oversubscribed; the style-fit discount (0.93) reflects real risk of racing in a compromised position, and recent form on good going has been modest.|

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up sprinter with a fade flag; won over 5f on good and shows ability at that distance, but 73 days off and the fade tendency makes 6f in a hot-pace race questionable.|

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old with a win over 5f on good going, but the 7-day turnaround is very quick and the form over 6f has been patchy; seven-pound claimer Terry Casey adds inexperience in traffic.|

runners_data.name: Dawn Romance
runners_data.note: Colin Keane on a prominent-style three-year-old who won over 6f on good ground — the trainer has four winners in the last 15 days showing good form, and Keane's positional intelligence in congested fields is a genuine asset.|

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent runner dropping slightly in class with a prior 6f win on good going, but ten runs without a win recently and trainer cold for past two weeks.|

runners_data.name: Leveraging
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who makes the pace but whose good-going figures are limited and who has struggled to convert on similar surfaces; Robbie Colgan must manage three-way lead rivalry, which could prove self-defeating.|

runners_data.name: Grande Cuvee
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has placed in three of four career starts including on good ground over 6f — the most consistently placed of the three leaders and could prove the most resilient if the pace war unfolds in front.|

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old from the Marnane yard with a win on good ground; form over 6f has shown improvement and the 18-day gap is fine, though consistency has been elusive.|

runners_data.name: All The Girls
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old who handles good-to-soft but has limited good-ground form; James Ryan rides and the horse has placed twice over 6f at shorter distances — finding the right position will be everything.|

runners_data.name: My Cubby Bear
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old returning from a 299-day absence — lengthy layoff makes form assessment almost impossible and this looks like a fitness outing in a tough 25-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from Evanna McCutcheon; all recent form is over 7f and dropping to 6f for the first time in a while is a question mark, though the horse has placed twelve times in fifteen starts on good going.|

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type by profile, with two wins in the last five on good going — the redistribution into midfield means the horse is genuinely likely to race between roles; style-fit discount applies and that limits confidence however strong the raw form figures appear.|

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose good-going form over 6f has produced zero wins from nine tries on similar; Patrick Foley sends out Tokyo Treasure too, creating stable questions, and the 8-day turnaround is tight.|

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Squeezed out of its natural hold-up slot into midfield on this map because hold-up positions are oversubscribed — the horse has four places in the last five on good ground and is consistent, but the compromised role (STYLE_FIT 0.90) dampens expectation.|

runners_data.name: Pinar Del Rio
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent runner with solid placed form but an eight-race winless run on good going; Declan McDonogh gives it a competent pilot but the age and form trajectory are not encouraging.|

runners_data.name: The Bear Trap
runners_data.note: 492 days off the course is an enormous absence; won over 7f on AW and has some placed form over 7f, but 6f on turf fresh off such a break looks very tough in this company.|

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Genuinely a prominent-style runner by nature, pushed into a midfield map position because prominent slots are oversubscribed in this field; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) acknowledges it cannot realistically get its preferred spot, and recent form has not been convincing.|

races.paceDynamic: Leveraging, Grande Cuvee and Venetian Star are all confirmed front-runners in a 25-runner field, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over Cork's flat six furlongs with no scope for a tactical crawl. The ten prominent-style runners crowding behind them will create a wall of horse early, generating traffic danger and interference between the two- and three-furlong markers that will cost several midfield runners momentum at a critical stage. With pace burning from the front and congestion through the middle sectors, the race is set up to suit hold-up horses who can find clear daylight late — provided they are genuine closers and not horses pushed to the back from a naturally prominent style. The field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can honestly accommodate at the rear: Mehman, Cashel Blue and Nouvel Espoir are redistributed into midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning true late-running beneficiaries are fewer than the raw numbers suggest, and the runners most likely to secure the prominent position against the three leaders are Real Encounter, Dawn Romance and All The Girls, who have the strongest claims to track the pace cleanly. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses with a decisive late burst who can sidestep the traffic, and jockeys with the patience to wait for gaps — not those squeezed into an unnatural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Closers Storm
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners force a strong honest gallop that burns off the prominent pack and leaves a vacuum for hold-up horses to fill late.
scenarios.body: Leveraging, Grande Cuvee and Venetian Star fight for supremacy and cook each other, leaving the field strung out and tiring entering the final furlong while genuine closers deliver from off the pace. Jon Riggens, Go Athletico and Sommelier are the profile horses — experienced hold-up sprinters on going they handle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survives Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent-position horse breaks cleanly, avoids the early congestion and tucks in just behind the leaders to strike at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With the front-runners burning fuel, the horse who finds the ideal position just off the pace without burning energy in traffic becomes the effective pace-setter into the straight. Real Encounter and Dawn Romance both have the profile — sharp enough to be prominent, proven at the trip, and ridden by experienced handlers in Foley and Keane.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three confirmed front-runners gets a soft lead through the first two furlongs while rivals jostle for position behind.
scenarios.body: In a field this large the three leaders may paradoxically neutralise each other's tactical threat early, and with 22 horses behind in chaos, one front-runner could steal a break and control fractions enough to last. Grande Cuvee's consistent placed form in front-running style and Leveraging's experience make them the most likely survivalists if the pace is miscalculated.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Winner
scenarios.trigger: If severe traffic interference eliminates most of the hold-up and prominent runners, producing a messy, attritional finish where a midfield horse picks through the wreckage.
scenarios.body: Redistributed hold-up types Cashel Blue and Mehman are racing out of their natural role and carry a style-fit discount, making this the least reliable shape to engineer deliberately. Nouvel Espoir, though also redistributed, has consistent placed form in similar-going sprints and could benefit if gaps appear at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: With Leveraging, Grande Cuvee and Venetian Star all in the same 25-runner field, watch for jostling and bumping in the first two furlongs as three genuine front-runners collide for the same strip of ground — one or more may be knocked sideways or forced back, altering the entire race shape.

The ten prominent-position runners behind the leaders create a wall of traffic between two and three furlongs out — watch for hold-up horses like Jon Riggens and Go Athletico being trapped behind horses who have no room to let them through.

Whiskey And Beer returns from 760 days off with a fade flag in a fast-run sprint — this horse is a danger to others rather than a threat to the result, watch for it weakening sharply and causing interference in the final furlong.

Mehman and Cashel Blue are racing out of their natural hold-up role into midfield due to redistribution — if either attempts to drop back to find cover they risk being completely detached, so watch how their jockeys manage the first furlong.

My Cubby Bear (299 days absent) and The Bear Trap (492 days absent) are both prominent-style runners returning from very long layoffs — monitor their warm-up behaviour and early running as fitness unknowns in a field this size.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Follow Us On X Handicap

runners_data.name: Green Kite
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner prone to fading late; 63 days off is a concern, and sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 4 Good-ground runs at this sort of trip makes it hard to get excited despite Colin Keane aboard.

runners_data.name: Spent All Me Money
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but has the best recent placed form on Good ground of any in this race (3rd last time, 2W4P in sim-going), with headgear (p) in place; Conor Lamon's 10lb claim helps off OR 58.

runners_data.name: Battleforsupremacy
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for a yard with one winner in 17 over 14 days; hold-up runner whose best form came at STA, and only three Good-ground runs have yielded zero wins or places — trip and course are modest questions.

runners_data.name: Lilbittyprettyone
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fading tendency, all five recent runs at 5f or 8f — the 7f trip here is an untested middle ground; 0W0P on Good and form figures of 9-9-6-8-5 are not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner with a strong profile for this shape — three recent placed efforts at 7f on Good ground (5th, 4th, 2nd), and Siobhan Rutledge has ridden her before; trainer McConnell hits form (T14: 3/28).

runners_data.name: Frosted Sky
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type with a fading flag; all Good-ground starts have produced finishes of 13th, 6th and 8th with no place, and stepping back to 7f after a 37-day break is not straightforward.

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination (Andrew Slattery) in very sharp form (7/23 in 14 days), and nine days between runs suggests cherry-ripe freshness; genuine hold-up runner over 8f who drops in trip — stamina will convert to a strong finish if 7f tests rivals.

runners_data.name: Gilts
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who does fade but has a course win at 7f on Good ground and a place to go with it — Jack Cleary's 5lb claim helps; form of 07918 shows a peak of 1st is possible in the right conditions.

runners_data.name: Lust
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose natural position is the rear of the field — pushed into midfield on the map simply because the race is over-populated with closers; Good-ground record at 8-10f is modest (0W1P in 15), and 8 days between runs is fine but stepping down to 7f is a worry.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with an outstanding Good-ground record (13/15 sim-going, 0W6P) who consistently runs his race — 9 days between runs is fine; OR 48 and a 5lb claim for Rory Mulligan makes this one of the best-fit profiles for the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan adds class, but this is genuinely a hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map because the rear is full; best form on Good ground came at 8f (1 win), and dropping to 7f in a 25-runner field with headgear (tp) is a test of adaptability.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type whose Good-ground record spans 5 places from 15 runs — veteran campaigner pushed into midfield on the map rather than ridden from behind; 55 days since last run is the standout concern.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and carries a redistribution flag; Denis Hogan has been quiet (0/23 in 14 days) and nine best finishes on Good ground are 9th or worse — the combination of trainer form and finishing tendency makes this hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Linger For Longer
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse whose true style is rear of field — 91 days off is the biggest flag in the race; WJ Lee is a quality booking but a form string of 60-040 and 12 months of Good-ground mediocrity does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consecutive places at 7f and 8f on Good ground (3rd, 2nd) — trainer Slattery in firing form (T14: 7/23) gives this a live angle; Adam Browne-Souza's 7lb claim is significant and this is one of the better prominent profiles to track Haroussa.

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was placed at 2nd over 7f on Good ground last time for Paddy Harnett (3lb claim); headgear (tp) retained and 46 days off is manageable — form tailed off in longer trips, so this return to 7f looks well-timed.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare placed in midfield on the map because of field congestion; a 4th and a 6th on Good ground are her best recent efforts and Chris Hayes is a quality booking — but the fading tendency and redistribution mean she needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Pick A Window
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who fades late, mapped here to midfield only because there is no room at the back; best recent effort was a 5th over 7f on Good for this trainer (O'Donnell, 0/0 in 14 days) — 49 days off and headgear (p) add uncertainty.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan is a significant booking for Laura Hourigan's charge; this fading hold-up type has a 3rd on Good over 6f in recent form and headgear (t) is retained — genuine hold-up runner who cannot get her natural position in this field.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader who has been racing at 5-6f — the step up to 7f is untried in recent form; Daniel McLoughlin has one winner from 17 in 14 days and 15th on her last Good-ground start does not encourage.

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.note: All five Good-ground runs have produced a best of 6th — the form record shows no ability to compete at this level; fading tendency and redistribution to midfield compound the challenges for a lightly-raced 3-year-old.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader mapped into midfield; nine is the best Good-ground finish from seven qualifying runs and Conor Maxwell has been quiet (0/11 in 14 days) — 7 days between runs is fine but the evidence for this horse making an impact is thin.

runners_data.name: Strikepoint
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield by field congestion, with a fading flag and no jockey declared; best recent effort is 7th on Good and the absence of a rider confirmation at this stage is a live risk.

runners_data.name: Haroussa
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, trained by JP Murtagh (2/25 in 14 days) — she will lead uncontested but her only three runs have all produced fading finishes and she has never led a field of 25; the prominent/lead role suits the race shape but the finishing tendency is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades — a true rear-of-field runner forced into midfield on the map by sheer numbers; headgear (p) is worn and trainer Sweeney has been quiet (0/1 in 14 days), with best recent form on Good ground a 5th at 8f.

races.paceDynamic: Haroussa is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 25-horse field and, crucially, faces no serious challenger for the lead — Whatswrongnow and the other prominent types (Sayonara, Liamo) are unlikely to match Haroussa's early speed and will slot in behind rather than contest the pace. With one horse controlling from the front at a sustainable tempo on Good ground over 7f at Cork, the pace will be honest but not punishing, giving Haroussa a chance to ration her effort and potentially steal a break on the field. The field is grossly overpopulated with hold-up horses — Lust, Strikepoint, Sceitimini, Cannonball Queen, She's On The Ball and others are genuine come-from-behind types who have been pushed into the midfield map position simply because there is no room at the rear of 25 runners; they will not all be able to travel in their preferred position and some will be forced wider or closer than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: with a lone, uncontested pace-setter operating at a sustainable tempo, the race shape favours prominent stalkers who can track Haroussa and pounce in the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who will need a strong, end-to-end gallop to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Haroussa Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Haroussa gets a clean break, leads uncontested and the prominent stalkers fail to close the gap entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Haroussa sets a controlled, sustainable pace and the field is too congested mid-race for closers to find clear runs in time; the prominent stalkers who tracked her — Whatswrongnow and Princess Chloe — are best placed to pounce but Haroussa's head start is decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Haroussa's pace is just honest enough to be reeled in and the prominent trackers (Whatswrongnow, Sayonara, Liamo) close within a length at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Whatswrongnow's solid record on Good ground and Sayonara's consistent placed form suit a race where they can track a single pace-setter and produce a sustained finish; Princess Chloe, with multiple placed efforts at 7f on Good, is also ideally positioned to challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest, the field strings out and a compact finisher from the redistributed midfield group finds a gap and runs on strongly.
scenarios.body: Spent All Me Money has the best recent Good-ground placed form of those mapped to midfield and could produce a late rattle if the pace stretches the field; Cisterna's trainer is in hot form (T14: 7/23) and nine days fresh could mean she is cherry-ripe to deliver.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace develops into an end-to-end gallop and every hold-up horse is able to settle, switch off and produce a storming late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario is inherently low probability because the true hold-up types (Lust, Cannonball Queen, Sceitimini) have all been redistributed from the rear to midfield and will not race in their natural comfort zone; if one does manage to find the rails and a clean run, Cannonball Queen's 4th and 6th on recent Good ground make her the most plausible beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Haroussa (sole front-runner) is uncontested but has finished 9th, 5th and 11th in three career starts — watch whether she maintains her gallop past the 2f pole or visibly weakens and hands the initiative to Whatswrongnow or Sayonara.
Whatswrongnow and Sayonara are the two prominent types best placed to track Haroussa — watch the early positions as the field jumps;

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse wearing a tongue-tie, 49 days off; showed a placed effort over 7f on good ground but has struggled in big-field 8f handicaps — the traffic risk in a 21-runner field is significant.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with a recent win over 8f on good ground (OR 66) for Adrian McGuinness; wore a visor, 13 days ago, and the sim-going record of 1W4P from 15 outings confirms he handles these conditions as well as anyone in the field.

runners_data.name: Greek Flower

runners_data.name: Star Strewn

runners_data.name: Storm Averted
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse at heart whose best form comes from the rear, but with so many closers in this field it has been mapped to midfield — Adam Browne-Souza's 7lb claim helps, yet the style mismatch (STYLE_FIT 0.92) tempers confidence in a field this size.

runners_data.name: Elusive Duke
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on this four-year-old who has placed five times from 15 runs on good ground; an authentic hold-up type pushed into midfield by the weight of closers in this race, meaning the finishing kick that produces those placed efforts may not arrive on time (STYLE_FIT 0.93).

runners_data.name: Trumph
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, making the hold-up tag a concern — Shane Foley rides but recent form reads 8-0-6-0 and there is no evidence of finishing strongly at this trip on good ground.

runners_data.name: Coasting
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for David Marnane, 117 days absent — the lengthy layoff combined with no placed form at 8f on good ground makes this a speculative entry in a 21-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Holy Lettuce
runners_data.note: Unknown running style for K J Condon with W J Lee aboard; placed at 8f on good ground last time and the unknown-style tag means it could be a factor if it happens to sit in a favourable position — the form trend is quietly consistent.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point

runners_data.name: Sherekiya

runners_data.name: Navagio

runners_data.name: Wegotogether

runners_data.name: Little Miss P

runners_data.name: Expound
runners_data.note: Top-rated in the field at OR 72, confirmed front-runner for Denis Hogan wearing both a tongue-tie and cheekpieces; 25 days off and stepping down from longer trips, but the front-running profile and equipment combination suggest he will boss the early stages at Cork over this flat mile.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood with two wins from 15 runs on good ground for Ms Claire O'Connell; 8 days since last run at OR 60 — the lowest rating in the field — but the natural prominent style and the fact she ran second over 8f on good ground recently make her one of the better-placed tactical runners.

races.paceDynamic: Expound and Star Strewn are the two confirmed front-runners in a 21-runner field, and both will be keen to establish position from the off, creating a genuinely contested lead that should produce an honest, pressure-filled gallop throughout the mile on good ground at Cork. Star Strewn has been racing prominently at Sligo and steps up to this distance, while Expound — the higher-rated of the pair at OR 72 — brings front-running habits reinforced by tongue-tie and a cheekpiece combination. With the field carrying a heavy surplus of hold-up horses — Storm Averted, Elusive Duke, Wegotogether, All Hail, Cladach, Navajo Point, Navagio, and Little Miss P are all true closers redistributed into midfield because they cannot all get their preferred rear position in a 21-runner handicap — the genuine hold-up division is badly congested and will find it hard to land a meaningful late blow. The race shape strongly favours horses that can track the pace in a prominent or close-midfield position and stay on stoutly through the closing stages, particularly those with proven course-and-distance form on good ground who will not be shuffled back into the traffic that will clog the rear of this large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Expound and Star Strewn fight it out up front and the honest gallop stretches the field, rewarding those who track the pace efficiently.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a pressured but sustainable tempo on good ground over the mile, and the race develops into a stamina test where the horse with the best position entering the straight wins. Horses tracking in second or third gear — Go Out, Gloriously Glam, Autumn Twist — are perfectly placed to pounce as the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Expound or Star Strewn is allowed to dictate at a comfortable clip and the contested element dies away early.
scenarios.body: One front-runner — most likely Expound given the higher rating and handler's course-and-distance record — finds a rhythm and is never seriously pressured despite the initial challenge, drawing on reserves in the final two furlongs. Good ground and a flat track at Cork suits a front-runner who can conserve energy through the middle portion of the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Close-Midfield Swoopers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other off and a properly-placed close-midfield tracker produces a decisive late burst in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop softens both lead horses inside the final two furlongs, opening the race up for horses sitting fourth to eighth who have been shielded from the early pressure. Comfort Line and Sherekiya have the profile — both race at this trip on good ground regularly and carry form to match — while Holy Lettuce is unknown-style but showed a placed effort at the distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the redistribution advantage dissolves, allowing genuine hold-up types to pick their way through.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability shape precisely because so many true closers — Elusive Duke, Storm Averted, Wegotogether — are unlikely to secure their natural rearward position in a 21-runner field and will race out of role, blunting their finishing kicks. Only if the front two set a genuinely suicidal pace do any of the rerouted hold-up horses find enough daylight to deliver a meaningful challenge.

watchPoints.text: Expound and Star Strewn will fight for the lead from the gates — watch the opening furlong for how vigorously they contest it, as a brutal early duel could set up the race for the prominent trackers and destroy both their chances.

The true hold-up division — Storm Averted, Elusive Duke, Wegotogether, All Hail, Cladach, Navajo Point, Navagio, and Little Miss P — will be jostling for position in a 21-runner field with far fewer gaps than their jockeys would like; watch for traffic problems approaching the straight.
Cladach ran just one day ago — monitor the pre-race ring for any signs of fatigue or lack of freshness; if the horse looks flat, discount it entirely regardless of Declan McDonogh's presence.

Go Out and Gloriously Glam are the two most naturally placed prominent types behind the front-runners — watch their positions at the halfway mark; if either is sitting third to fifth with cover, they are live dangers to the front two.

Holy Lettuce is listed as unknown style for K J Condon with W J Lee — watch where W J Lee positions the horse in the first two furlongs, as the unknown-style tag means it could be racing prominently or midfield, and the outcome of its race depends entirely on which it turns out to be.
